briefing.headline: OpenAI's o4 model sparks new arms race as China accelerates open-source frontier push

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has intensified with multiple frontier labs releasing advanced reasoning models in August. Geopolitical tensions are driving record compute investments while safety concerns mount around agentic systems. Prompt injection remains the dominant exploit vector across deployed applications.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with 2.1T parameters and native multi-agent orchestration. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus achieved new SOTA on GPQA while Google DeepMind's Gemini 3 introduced real-time video reasoning. xAI's Grok-3 and DeepSeek-R2 both launched within 72 hours of each other.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agentic AI but lack enforcement mechanisms.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced $15B hyperscale expansion in Texas and Arizona. TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips for NVIDIA and AMD. Oracle and CoreWeave signed multi-year capacity deals exceeding 100k H100 equivalents.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a Western lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
